docs.title: OpenTracker (syamajala fork)
docs.text:
OpenTracker is an open-source, clean-room firmware for the original Polyend Tracker, written from behavioural specifications. It contains no Polyend code, fonts, icons or graphics, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Polyend.

This fork follows upstream OpenTracker's 2.x line (currently 2.2.1) and adds features on top. Projects stay compatible: the fork's additions are stored in extra files next to project.mt, so stock firmware, upstream OpenTracker and the Tracker Mini still open them.

These are the docs for main

The site shows the documentation of the development branch. Once the fork makes releases, a version picker at the top selects the docs that match your image.

docs.title: What this fork adds
docs.text: Feature In short DX7 synth A 6-operator FM engine that plays Yamaha DX7 voices from .syx banks. Live resampling Record the master, one track or Line in while the pattern keeps playing; slice the take and place it on a track. Performance mode A bank of 16 scenes with a crossfader, and master FX (DJ filter, tape stop) played from the pads. Song mode Repeat counts, a Performance scene per song slot, and fader ramps between scenes. MIDI instrument LFO A tempo-locked LFO per MIDI instrument: CC, pitch bend or pressure. MIDI presets Save a synth's MIDI setup (CC slots with names, LFO) and load it into any MIDI instrument. More Note names (sharps / flats / auto), piano pads, plus a summary of the 2.x features from upstream. Remote control Drive a Tracker from a computer: scripts, screen text, a live mirror.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Installing, and getting back to stock firmware: Install and go back.
  • Something went wrong: Troubleshooting.
  • Building, testing or contributing: the Developers section.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• The synth engines are our own design: their settings follow the Tracker Mini, and the sound is close but not identical.
  • WTFM has no engine yet (its patches load and save, but stay silent). Wavetable and granular samples play the left channel only.
  • Synth notes ignore the per-track Performance columns (#30); the master FX do include them.
  • The synth voice pool defaults to 4 voices because of the processor's speed.
  • USB Storage mode: back up the card before first use.
  • The USB ID is the pid.codes test ID 1209:0001.

Screenshots in these docs come from the desktop simulator, which runs the same code as the firmware.

docs.title: Get an image
docs.text:
The firmware image is a single file named like PolyendTrackerOTv212.ptf (for version 2.2.1). Three ways to get one:

  • Releases: tagged versions are published on the fork's Releases page. (No release has been made yet.)
  • CI builds: every push to main builds an image. Open the latest CI run on main and download the firmware-… artifact (you need to be logged in to GitHub).
  • Build it yourself: see Building.

Keep the file name

The Tracker's update bootloader only accepts names of exactly 24 characters. Don't rename the .ptf file.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Copy the .ptf file to the /Firmware folder on the Tracker's SD card (or use USB Storage mode to copy it without taking the card out).
  2. On the Tracker, go to Config > Firmware update, select the file and confirm.
  3. If the screen stays dark after the update, press the power button once.

docs.title: Go back to stock firmware
docs.text:
Keep Polyend's stock image, PolyendTracker_1.9.2.ptf, in /Firmware too. Then either:

  • install it the same way, from Config > Firmware update, or
  • if OpenTracker doesn't start: put the stock file's name in a text file /Firmware/ot_restore.txt and power-cycle the Tracker. This check runs before anything else in OpenTracker, so it works even when the rest of the firmware doesn't.

Keep /Firmware tidy

The rear reset button installs a random .ptf from /Firmware. Keep only the image you want plus the stock one there.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
• Projects are saved in the Tracker Mini 2.2.1 format (16-track patterns, three synth slots). Older original-Tracker projects open as they are, with tracks 13–16 empty.
  • The fork's additions (Performance scenes, song counts and scenes, MIDI LFOs) are stored in extra files next to project.mt. Stock firmware, upstream OpenTracker and the Tracker Mini ignore them and open the project normally.
  • Stock firmware for the original Tracker reads only tracks 1–8 of 2.x projects (expected from the stock loader's rules; not yet confirmed on a stock unit).

docs.title: Firmware
docs.text:
Needs the Arm GNU toolchain (arm-none-eabi-gcc; CI uses 14.2.Rel1) and Python 3.

make clean
make -j VERSION=2.2.1

This writes build/opentracker.elf, build/opentracker.hex and the flashable image build/PolyendTrackerOTv212.ptf.

Change VERSION? Run make clean first

Objects aren't rebuilt when only VERSION changes, so the image would report the old version. Check with strings build/opentracker.elf | grep -x 2.2.1.

The image name must be exactly 24 characters (the update bootloader rejects other lengths), so it carries the version digits only.

docs.title: Build options
docs.text: Option Builds OT_GAMES=1 an image with Games (off by default in this fork: it frees 5.8 KB of SRAM and ~49 KB of flash); build dir build/games OT_STACK_GUARD_TEST=1 a stack guard test image: with /Firmware/ot_guardtest.txt on the card it overflows the stack once on purpose, and the next boot logs PASSED / FAILED; build dir build/guardtest SELFTEST=1 a hardware bring-up image that always runs the selftest OT_SDRAM_CACHE=0, OT_FASTRUN=0, OT_USB_MSC=0 diagnostic variants (no SDRAM cache, all audio code in flash, no USB mass storage)

docs.title: Size checks
docs.text:
python3 tools/telemetry_check.py size --size-tool arm-none-eabi-size build/opentracker.elf
python3 tools/telemetry_check.py frames build
  • Flash (.text + .data): fails above 800,000 B, warns above 720,000 B (upstream fails at 720,000 B; the fork's DX7, remote control and Performance mode need more). The image itself may not pass 877,664 B, the stock 1.9.2 extent (tools/check_image.py).
  • Stack headroom (_estack − _ebss): fails below 75 KiB.
  • libm: fails if double-precision math functions get linked.
  • Frames: fails if any single function's stack frame is as large as the stack guard (8 KB) or unbounded, warns above 75 % of it.

docs.title: Host tests
docs.text:
The core (src/core) is platform-independent and tested on the host with a C++17 compiler (CI uses GCC 14, with AddressSanitizer and UBSan):

make host-test

It builds and runs the tests on every core (nproc); HOST_JOBS=N sets the number of jobs, HOST_JOBS=1 runs them one by one.

On some kernels AddressSanitizer needs sudo sysctl -w vm.mmap_rnd_bits=28. A newer GCC can miss warnings that GCC 14 reports (CI builds with -Werror); to reproduce CI exactly: make -C tests CXX="g++ -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2".

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text:
make -C sim
build/sim/opentracker-sim

Needs SDL2 (and ALSA for MIDI). See Simulator.

docs.title: Test songs
docs.text:
make testsongs

Builds nine OT Test songs and seven BLAST GRID synth remixes into build/testsongs/. Copy its Projects/ and Samples/ folders to a card.

docs.title: Performance gate
docs.text:
make perf-gate [LOG=tracker.log]

Instruction counts of the audio engine on an emulated Cortex-M4 (QEMU) against tests/perf_baseline.txt (+5 % max) and per-engine limits, the flash and stack checks, a host benchmark, and, with LOG=, the telemetry thresholds of a device log. Needs qemu-system-arm for the M4 part (skipped otherwise). Run it for anything on the audio path.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: This site is built from docs/ in the repository with MkDocs and the Material theme, and published to GitHub Pages by .github/workflows/docs.yml.

docs.title: Edit and preview
docs.text:
Docs change in the same pull request as the feature they describe.

python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install "mkdocs<2" mkdocs-material mike
.venv/bin/mkdocs serve            # http://127.0.0.1:8000, reloads on save
.venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict   # what CI runs: broken links fail

Pages are listed in mkdocs.yml (nav:). Images go in docs/images/.

docs.title: Screenshots
docs.text:
Screenshots come from the simulator, so they can be regenerated whenever a screen changes:

make testsongs && make -C sim
tools/docs_screens.sh            # all of them, or: tools/docs_screens.sh song performance

Each shot in tools/docs_screens.sh is a short simulator script run on a fresh scratch card: either the generated test songs with "BG World 1" open, or an empty project with a generated example DX7 bank. No third-party content goes into the images.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
Publishing uses mike, which keeps one copy of the site per version on the gh-pages branch:

  • every push to main updates dev;
  • once the fork makes releases, each release tag will add its version, and the version picker at the top will switch between them.

docs.title: OpenTracker memory audit: fork vs upstream 2.1.2
docs.text: 2026-10-23. Measured from the ELF images (Games off) and on a Tracker over the remote-control link. Fork: syamajala/polyend-tracker-re main (a8ac7b4, on 2.1.1); upstream: sandlbn/polyend-tracker-re v2 at 2.1.2 (177150b). Fork figures corrected the same day from clean builds: the first version listed the fork's room above _ebss as upstream's.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Upstream is at its limits on both RAMs. It has 1,104 B free in .sdram_bss and 1,280 B over its 90 KiB stack rule.
  • Most of that pressure is fixed cost, not features. A per-screen buffer for each browser list, the screens on the SRAM heap, and a stack rule set without measurement account for tens of KB.
  • The fork's fixed SRAM is about 1 KB more than upstream's (169,412 B vs 168,420 B), even with its extra features. Our margin comes from measuring the real stack use, putting the screens in SDRAM and sharing the browser buffers.
  • Ready to merge: branch feature/sdram-shared-lists (off upstream/v2, two commits) frees 16 KB of .sdram_bss and 8.4 KB of heap on upstream.
  • These fixes don't need a module system. They are independent of the modular-architecture discussion and can land first. A module system mainly helps flash (features in or out of a build); on its own it doesn't reduce these fixed RAM costs.

docs.title: SRAM (256 KB)
docs.text:
Upstream 2.1.2 Fork main Audio code run from SRAM (.fastrun) 40,248 B 41,424 B Other initialised data 2,904 B 7,016 B .bss 102,580 B 98,284 B DMA + USB buffers 22,688 B 22,688 B Fixed SRAM total 168,420 B 169,412 B Room above _ebss (heap + stack) 93,440 B 92,448 B Link-time stack rule (STACK_MIN) 92,160 B (90 KiB) 76,800 B (75 KiB) Margin over the rule 1,280 B 15,648 B Screens (ScreenSet) on the heap 15,884 B 0 (in SDRAM) Stack guard + heap reserve — 12,288 B Stack really left at run time ~77.5 KB ~80 KB

Measured on a Tracker (fork, stack painting + telemetry):

Value Deepest stack use 18,084 B (long session: project load and play, Sample Editor effects, Save / Save As, resample, USB storage) Typical 11–12.5 KB Heap 232 B once the screens are in SDRAM Deepest single frame 6,032 B (-fstack-usage, every function)

So about 60 KB of the stack is never touched. The 90 KiB rule is what's tight, not the stack itself.

docs.title: SDRAM (16 MB)
docs.text:
The fixed layout is the same in both: about 11.25 MB of sample pool, 1.56 MB for delay and reverb, and patterns, undo, clipboard, Performance, stems and the remote frame buffer. It ends a little below .sdram_bss.

.sdram_bss Upstream 2.1.2 Upstream + sdram-shared-lists Fork main today Region 92 KB @ 0x70FD9000 92 KB 148 KB @ 0x70FDB000 Used 93,104 B 77,056 B 90,960 B Free 1,104 B 17,152 B 60,592 B Unused SDRAM above the region 64 KB 64 KB 0

The SDRAM above the region is used only by the self-test's SD benchmark, which never runs alongside the app.

docs.title: Recommendations for upstream, by payoff
docs.text:
1. Merge feature/sdram-shared-lists (a034a95, 6b0ccaa).
  2. Shared browser lists: the Sample Loader, Synth patch browser, File Open/Save, Import Mod and firmware-update lists share one buffer (browserListMem(), 11,400 B). Only one is ever on screen, and each rebuilds its list when it opens.
  3. One screenshot row buffer: the row is converted to BMP bytes in place.
  4. Result: .sdram_bss −16,048 B, heap −8.4 KB, flash −344 B. All 91 upstream test suites and make -C sim check pass. In the fork it's device-tested by a remote script that visits every list (24 checks).
  5. Screens in SDRAM (fork 928db9d, feature/screens-sdram). ScreenSet moves from the heap into .sdram_bss, which frees the remaining ~7.5 KB of heap after step 1. Device-tested: render and loop times were identical while browsing a 578-file folder with previews.
  6. Base the stack rule on measurement.
  7. Measure: paint the stack and report the peak in telemetry.
  8. Guard: add a SYSMPU guard below the stack (fork #34: 8 KB; an overflow locks up the core, resets, and is reported on the next boot).
  9. Check frames: a CI check that fails if a single frame could jump over the guard (telemetry_check.py frames).
  10. Then lower the rule. The fork went from 90 to 75 KiB, which frees about 15 KB of SRAM at link time without moving anything.
  11. Keep the Open's Project off the stack, with one spare copy (fork ac02790, with 51d9f57). Upstream keeps a Project on the stack in startOpenProject and in the Workspace load step, plus ProjectJob::proj. One SDRAM jobProject_ outside the job state replaces all three. That's no extra SDRAM, two big stack frames fewer, and one copy fewer.
  12. Grow .sdram_bss into the unused 64 KB above it. It's a linker-script and board.h size change, plus a static_assert that the region stays below the end of SDRAM.

Only if SRAM is still needed:

Candidate Saves Condition Instruments to SDRAM ~17 KB Read at note-on; needs a CPU check SD bounce buffer ~16 KB Only once SDHC → SDRAM DMA is verified Diagnostic log ring ~8 KB Shrink it, or move it after boot .fastrun code back to flash varies Each piece costs audio CPU

docs.title: Tools used
docs.text:
• tools/size_report.py: flash, SRAM sections, .sdram_bss, stack headroom and free space, base vs head. Runs as a CI job summary on every PR.
  • tools/telemetry_check.py:
  • size: the link-time limits;
  • frames: the deepest frame vs the stack guard;
  • log: stack peak, heap, CPU and overruns from a device log.
  • -fstack-usage on every build; pahole -C <type> build/opentracker.elf for struct layouts.
  • Remote-control scripts (tools/remote_scripts/*.txt), run on the simulator in CI and on a Tracker with the telemetry log captured.

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text:
The desktop simulator runs the same platform-independent core (src/core) as the firmware on Linux, with host implementations of the hardware interfaces: an SDL2 window with the screen, pads and keys, audio out, ALSA MIDI, and a folder as the SD card. Most features can be developed and tested without flashing.

The full reference is sim/README.md.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
make -C sim
build/sim/opentracker-sim [--sd DIR] [--scale 2] [--line-in]
  • --sd DIR is the SD card root (default ~/.opentracker-sd, created on first run). The workspace is saved there when the window closes; Config is kept in DIR.eeprom.
  • Keyboard: F1–F8 are the screen keys, arrows, Space = Play, Shift, Delete, Page Up / Down = encoder. Tab switches between command mode (letters = module keys, e.g. 2 Performance, 0 Song) and pad mode (letter rows = pads). The mouse works on every control; right-click latches a button (e.g. Shift).

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text:
Without a window (--script FILE and/or --screenshot OUT.png), time is virtual: every simulated millisecond is one app loop pass, so runs are deterministic and fast.

wait 300               # advance time (ms)
tap PERFORMANCE        # press and release a button (names: src/core/ui/buttons.h)
press SHIFT / release SHIFT
hold F5 400
pad 12 tap             # pads 0..47
enc 3                  # encoder detents
screenshot perf.png

Plus checks (expect-screen, expect-sound, expect-playing …) and --wav OUT.wav to record the audio. make -C sim check runs the simulator's own checks.

docs.title: Display budgets
docs.text: The Tracker's display chip (FT813) has a small display-list memory (RAM_DL). The budget and fragcheck commands in sim/scripts/display_budget.txt and fork_screens.txt measure each screen's largest frame and check it looks identical with the fragment cache on and off. A new or changed screen needs an entry there.

docs.title: Standing in for a Tracker
docs.text:
• --serve acts like a Tracker with remote control on, on a pseudo-terminal, so tools/tracker_remote.py scripts run against it (CI does this).
  • --remote DEV and --mirror DEV use a real Tracker as the panel or show its screen: see Remote control.

docs.title: Testing and CI
docs.text: The rule of thumb: test in the simulator and on the host first, and use the device for what only hardware shows (sound quality and clicks, real CPU and stack use, pads and LEDs, the codec and Line in, SD timing). Batch device tests so one flash covers several changes.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text: Layer Command Covers Host tests make host-test ~100 test binaries: models, formats, sequencer, audio engines, UI screens, display budgets (ASan + UBSan) Simulator checks make -C sim check smoke runs, display budgets and fragment checks per screen, resampling end to end, the test songs open and play Remote scripts tools/sim_remote_check.sh tools/remote_scripts/*.txt against the simulator, each on a fresh card; the same files run on a Tracker M4 benchmark make perf-gate audio instruction counts on an emulated Cortex-M4 against a baseline, engine limits, size checks Device tools/tracker_remote.py, tools/telemetry_check.py log scripts and telemetry on a real Tracker

docs.title: Remote scripts
docs.text:
Scripts in tools/remote_scripts/ drive the app through tracker_remote.py and are written to run on both the simulator and a Tracker:

  • Wait on the sequencer, not the clock: wait-for pass == 2, wait-for slot == 3 20000, so a script works at any tempo.
  • A script's card starts with SCRIPT.sd/ (copy it to a Tracker's card too) and, in the simulator only, SCRIPT.sim-sd/.

On a device:

tools/tracker_remote.py /dev/ttyACM0 tools/remote_scripts/song_scene.txt --log tracker.log
tools/telemetry_check.py log tracker.log

tools/device_soak.txt is a navigation-only soak for a loaded project (no edits, saves or loads).

Gotchas when writing scripts:

  • Opening the Sample Recorder while a pattern plays pops a "stop the pattern?" dialog (Resample / Cancel / Yes) that takes the F keys. Stop playback first, or answer it.
  • Config reopens on the category it was last on, so start from a known place (e.g. Up × 7).
  • On a device, the diag ring drops early boot lines. Send a byte on the CDC port to replay the boot log.

docs.title: Hardware probes
docs.text:
A test image built with make OT_REMOTE_REGS=1 also answers register commands in drive mode, so hardware questions can be answered with a script instead of a special image. Release images (the default OT_REMOTE_REGS=0) answer every one of them with FAIL.

Script command Does Limited to peek ADDR [N] read N (1..8) MCU words GPIO, PORT, SIM, SRAM, flash (other peripherals fault when their clock is off) poke ADDR VALUE write an MCU word a PORTx_PCRn switching between disabled and GPIO input: a pin can never be made to drive ftrd ADDR [N] read N (1..32) bytes of display memory the FT81x memory map ftwr ADDR VALUE [BYTES] write a display register the register block, not REG_CPURESET or the coprocessor's FIFO pointers

Addresses and values are hex without 0x; the rules are in src/core/remote/remote.h. Python scripts can call Runner.peek / poke / ftrd / ftwr from tracker_remote.py. tools/int_n_probe.py uses them to find out whether the FT81x INT_N pin reaches the MCU (it toggles the pin and reads every port, then restores everything).

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
Pull requests and pushes to main run .github/workflows/ci.yml (other branches: Run workflow on the Actions tab):

Job Does host-tests make host-test with GCC 14, plus telemetry_check.py selftest sim-check builds the simulator, make -C sim check, the remote scripts; uploads screenshots firmware builds the image, size / stack / libm checks, the stack frame check; uploads the .ptf as an artifact size-report pull requests only: memory use of the PR against its base, as a table in the job summary

Error messages are shown as annotations on the run, so they're visible without opening the logs.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: Pushing a tag vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-suffix] (e.g. v2.1.2-ot1) runs .github/workflows/release.yml: host tests, the firmware with the size checks, and a GitHub release with the .ptf image. The image uses the numeric version only (v2.1.2-ot1 → PolyendTrackerOTv212.ptf); the suffix names the release.

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
• main is the fork's integration branch: what gets flashed and released. It's never rebased; upstream releases are merged into it.
  • v2 mirrors upstream's v2 (sandlbn/polyend-tracker-re) and is fast-forwarded when upstream moves.
  • Feature branches come into main through pull requests on the fork, with CI. A change meant for upstream starts from upstream/v2, so it can be offered upstream as it is; fork-only work (the DX7 engine, song scenes …) can start from main.
  • Upstream pull requests are opened one at a time. Upstream squash-merges, so a branch stacked on another is rebased after the first one lands.

docs.title: Merging an upstream release
docs.text:
1. Fast-forward the mirror: git push origin upstream/v2:v2.
  2. Merge upstream/v2 into a branch off main, resolve, then build with make clean and the new VERSION, run the host tests, make -C sim check and tools/sim_remote_check.sh.
  3. Open a pull request into main; flash it together with whatever else waits for a device test.

When upstream squash-merged one of our own pull requests, its conflicts resolve to our side, and only upstream's other changes need applying on top (git diff <their squash> <their release>).

docs.title: Compatibility rules
docs.text:
Projects must keep opening in stock firmware, upstream OpenTracker and the Tracker Mini:

  • Stock files keep their layout. project.mt, pattern files, .pti instruments and .patch files are written exactly as the stock / Mini formats define them.
  • Fork data goes into side files next to project.mt, which other firmware ignores:
File Holds perf_scenes.bin the Performance scene bank, A / B, and the fork's column types (DJ filter, tape stop, MIDI CC) and MIDI CC targets song.bin per-slot Count, Scene, Scene B and Ramp midi_lfo.bin one LFO per MIDI instrument .patch field 100 a DX7 voice (155 bytes), past every Mini field
  • Side files are versioned and written only when they hold something. The fork has no installed base yet, so their layouts can still change without migration code; stock compatibility can't.
  • A new Performance column type is not written into project.mt's type bytes (stock reads them); it lives in perf_scenes.bin, and stock sees an empty column.

docs.title: Code conventions
docs.text:
• src/core is platform-independent (shared by the firmware, the simulator and the host tests); src/hal is the K66 hardware layer.
  • Comments mark the origin of behaviour: [I] the fork's own (not in stock), spec references (spec 12 §E.2) for reverse-engineered stock behaviour.
  • The audio path has no allocation, no I/O and no locks. Anything on it goes through make perf-gate; new screens get a display budget entry.
  • No static constructors: a namespace-scope object or pointer must not need dynamic initialisation (for example T* const p = f(); with f() in another file). Use constexpr, an extern array with inline helpers, or set it up in start(). Check with arm-none-eabi-nm -C build/opentracker.elf | grep _GLOBAL__sub_I.

docs.title: DX7 synth
docs.text: A 6-operator FM engine that plays Yamaha DX7 voices, available as a sixth synth model next to ACD, FAT, VAP, WTFM and PERC. Thousands of free DX7 voices exist as SysEx (.syx) files; the Tracker plays them directly.

docs.title: Use a DX7 voice
docs.text:
1. Put .syx files in Patches/DX7/ on the SD card. Both kinds work:
    • 32-voice banks (4,104 bytes, the usual "bank" files);
    • single-voice dumps (163 bytes).
  2. Select a synth instrument (S1–S3): hold Instrument and turn the encoder.
  3. Press Instrument Params. On Synth Parameters, set Model to DX7 (it's the last entry in the list).
  4. Press Load Patch (F7).
  1. Banks come first in the list and open like folders: highlight one and press Open (F8). Pick a voice, Preview (F5, hold) to hear it, Confirm (F8) to load it. Left goes back to the bank list. Single-voice files sit with the patches and preview and load directly.

The loaded voice is named after the DX7 voice. Save (in Edit Patch) writes it as an ordinary .patch file in Patches/DX7/, with the voice stored inside it; the project keeps it too.

docs.title: Shape a voice
docs.text:
There's no operator editor yet, but Edit Patch has controls that work on top of any loaded voice, without changing the voice itself:

Section Control What it does Voice Volume The voice's level. Voice Mono For polyphony 1 slots: Retrigger (default) or Legato, see below. Tone Brightness ±100 %: the modulators' levels, ±12 dB. More or fewer harmonics. Tone Feedback ±7, added to the voice's own feedback (0–7). Tone Attack ±100 %: every operator's first envelope rate. + = slower. Tone Release ±100 %: every operator's release rate. + = longer tails. Tone LFO Depth 0–200 % of the voice's vibrato and tremolo, up to the DX7's maximum. Tone Detune 0–100 %: spreads the operators up to ±7 cents apart (chorus-like beating).

Each loaded DX7 voice comes with macros M1–M6 aimed at the six Tone controls and named after them (M1 Bright, M2 Feedback … M6 Detune). So a voice can be shaped from the Synth Macros page (Instrument Params again), or per step with the macro FX (columns A–F), without opening Edit Patch. The macros can still be re-aimed on their Edit Patch pages.

How much a control changes depends on the voice: Brightness does nothing on a voice without modulators, and Feedback is only heard when the feedback operator is audible.

docs.title: Playing
docs.text:
• DX7 slots play from any track like the other synths: notes, the step FX for pitch (Glide, Slide, Tune, Micro-tune), the Volume FX and the macro FX.
  • Polyphony is set on Synth Parameters. On a polyphony 1 slot, Mono decides what a new note does:
    • Retrigger (default): every note starts like a new voice, its envelopes from the beginning (without a click).
    • Legato: a note that overlaps the held one only moves the pitch; the envelopes run on, as on a DX7 in mono mode.
  • Velocity (the Volume step FX on a step with a note) works as on a DX7: through each operator's velocity sensitivity in the voice. On some voices it changes the level, on others mostly the tone (a velocity-sensitive modulator gets brighter with velocity). Voices whose operators have sensitivity 0 ignore it. To make one respond in level anyway, aim M7 (Velocity) at Volume on its Edit Patch page.
    • A Volume FX on a step without a note doesn't change a held DX7 note: velocity only counts when a note starts.
  • CPU: about 6 % per voice (estimated). The voice limiter cuts synth voices first if the audio gets close to its limit.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• The sound core is a port of Google's Music Synthesizer for Android (msfa, Apache 2.0), checked against Dexed note by note. Our additions: amplitude modulation, the feedback loops of algorithms 4 and 6, and key sync.
  • For deeper edits, edit the voice in a DX7 editor on a computer (Dexed works) and copy the .syx file over.
  • A Tracker Mini has no DX7 model: it resets a DX7 slot to its default when it opens the project.

docs.title: MIDI instrument LFO
docs.text: Each MIDI instrument (MIDI 1–16) gets one tempo-locked LFO, sent alongside its notes.

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
1. Select a MIDI instrument: hold Instrument and turn the encoder.
  2. Press Instrument Params, then Instrument Params again: the key steps through the MIDI parameters page, the MIDI Instrument LFO page and the MIDI Instrument Preset page.
Setting (key) Choices Target (F1) Off, one of the CC slots A–F, pitch bend or channel pressure; the whole list is on screen, slots shown by their CC's name ("A Cutoff"). The LFO follows the slot: change the slot's CC on the parameters page and the LFO moves with it. A slot set to Prg Chg or Poly AT sends nothing. Turning the encoder only picks the target; the LFO moves to it once the encoder rests, so the slots passed on the way are left alone. Shape (F2) Rev saw, Saw, Triangle, Square, Random. Rate (F3) From 128 steps per cycle down to 1/8 step, locked to the tempo. Depth (F4) How far it swings either side of Center, 0–64: Center 64 and Depth 32 sweep 32–96; Depth 64 sweeps the whole range. Center (F5) The value it swings around (0–127): value = Center + Depth × wave, kept within 0–127. On pitch bend, -64..63 around no bend, in the same steps as Depth. Retrigger (F6) Free (follows the song position) or Note (restarts with each note).

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• LFO messages use at most half of a DIN MIDI port's bandwidth, so notes are never delayed by them.
  • The LFO runs while the sequencer plays. At Stop, its target is left at Center, and so is a target you switch away from (or turn Off) while playing.
  • A step FX on the same target (the LFO's CC slot, pitch bend, or pressure) moves the LFO's Center, so the pattern can shift the wobble around.
  • Stored in midi_lfo.bin next to project.mt; other firmware ignores it.

docs.title: MIDI presets
docs.text:
A MIDI preset describes a synth: the names of its CCs (its CC chart, "74 Cutoff"), which CCs the six slots A–F use, velocity, offset and the MIDI LFO. Save it once, then load it into any MIDI instrument in any project.

The CC names show wherever a CC appears: as the slot name on the MIDI parameters page ("Cutoff" instead of "CC A"), in the CC A–F choice lists ("74 Cutoff") and as the LFO target. Step FX in the pattern still read CC A–F, as on the original firmware.

A preset describes the synth, not a sound or a channel:

  • No channel. It loads into whichever MIDI instrument is open, and that instrument's channel stays. A synth that listens on several channels (an Elektron Model:Cycles, one channel per track) uses one preset on each of them. Instruments that load the same preset share its CC chart, so a name changed on one shows on all of them.
  • No program change. To switch the synth's sound in a song, set a CC slot to Prg Chg and put that FX on a step.

docs.title: The Preset page
docs.text:
1. Select a MIDI instrument: hold Instrument and turn the encoder.
  2. Press Instrument Params until the title reads MIDI Instrument Preset (it steps through Parameters, LFO and Preset).

The left list is the CC chart: CC 0–127 with their names, and the letters of the slots that use each CC. It opens on slot A's CC. The right side shows the preset this instrument came from or was saved as, and the six slots.

Key Action Encoder, Up / Down Select a CC (hold Shift to move faster). F6 Name Name the selected CC (up to 9 characters). Delete Clear the selected CC's name. F1 Load List the presets on the card; the encoder or Up / Down move, F8 Load loads into this instrument, F7 Cancel closes the list. F2 Save Save under the preset's name (no name yet: as Save As). F3 Save As Save under a new name (asks before replacing a preset).

Which CC a slot uses is set on the MIDI parameters page, as before. The names and the preset name are saved with the project (midi_names.bin, next to project.mt), so project.mt stays readable by the original firmware. A project holds up to 400 CC names in all (about eight fully named synths).

docs.title: Presets that come with OpenTracker
docs.text:
Each release has a MidiPresets.zip: unzip it to the root of the card. It holds:

Preset Channels Slots A–F Model Cycles one per track (load it on each) Color, Shape, Sweep, Contour, Decay, Delay send Syntakt audio tracks 1–12 (Syn A–H = the machine's parameters) Cutoff, Reso, Filter env, Amp decay, Delay send, Reverb send Syntakt FX the FX track Filter freq, Filter reso, Drive, Delay mix, Reverb mix, Delay time volca fm2 its channel (needs MIDI RX ShortMessage on) Mod decay, Carrier decay, Algorithm, LFO rate, LFO pitch, Reverb SP-404MKII 1–4 = BUS 1–4, 5 = INPUT FX Ctrl 1–4, FX on, FX select S-1 its channel Cutoff, Reso, Filter env, Decay, Delay, Reverb

Each names every CC in the synth's MIDI chart. They are in midi_presets/ in the source; more synths are welcome.

docs.title: The preset file
docs.text:
Presets are text files in MidiPresets/ on the card, named <name>.txt, so they can be written or edited on a computer. For example, a Roland S-1:

# OpenTracker MIDI preset
velocity = 127
offset = 0
slot A = 74
slot B = 71
slot C = 24
slot D = 75
slot E = 92
slot F = 91
cc 3 = LFO Rate
cc 24 = Filt Env
cc 71 = Reso
cc 74 = Cutoff
cc 75 = Decay
cc 91 = Reverb
cc 92 = Delay
lfo target = slot A
lfo depth = 30
  • slot A … slot F: a CC number (0–127), PC (program change), AT (channel pressure) or PAT (poly aftertouch).
  • cc n = name: the name of CC n (0–127), up to 9 characters.
  • lfo target: off, slot A … slot F, PB (pitch bend) or AT. CC n also works: it picks the slot set to CC n.
  • lfo shape: 0 Rev saw, 1 Saw, 2 Triangle, 3 Square, 4 Random.
  • lfo rate: 0 (128 steps per cycle) to 22 (1/8 step), as listed on the LFO page.
  • lfo depth 0–64 (the swing either side of the center), lfo center 0–127, lfo retrigger 0 Free or 1 Note.

Lines starting with # are comments, keys ignore case, and a missing or unknown line keeps the default, so a preset can be as short as one cc line.

docs.title: Note names
docs.text: Config > General > Note names: Sharps / Flats / Auto. Auto spells notes the way the project's scale does, modes included: C Mixolydian shows B♭, not A♯. Display only.

docs.title: Piano pads
docs.text:
Config > General > Pad layout: Stock / Piano. Piano turns the pads into two keyboards that light up as ones, laid out as on grid controllers: each pair of rows is a keyboard, with the white keys along the lower row and the black keys in the row above, each black key over the white key to its right.

·  C# D# ·  F# G# A# ·  C# D# ·  F#     upper keyboard
C  D  E  F  G  A  B  C  D  E  F  G
·  C# D# ·  F# G# A# ·  C# D# ·  F#     lower keyboard
C  D  E  F  G  A  B  C  D  E  F  G
  • Each keyboard spans an octave and a fifth; the upper one is the same keyboard an octave higher.
  • The pads marked · (over C and F, where a piano has no black key) are dark and play nothing.
  • The bottom-left C is the C of the project's root note octave. To play higher or lower, change the root note.
  • The lights show the keyboard: the scale's root brightest, white keys lit, black keys a little dimmer. Keys outside the project's scale stay playable but are barely lit, so the scale shows on the keyboard.
  • It works wherever the pads play notes: the pattern editor's Note column, Sample Playback, the instrument pages, the synth browser, the Sample Editor and the recorder. In the pattern editor the step's note (and, with Pads preview, the notes on the current line) lights at full brightness.
  • Pads that do something else keep their own lights: the Instr and FX columns, Performance, the synth edit page, and Beat Slice instruments (one pad per slice).
  • Stock is the default and keeps the original layout. The setting is global, not saved with the project.

docs.title: Chord entry
docs.text:
In the pattern editor's edit mode (stopped), pads pressed while another note pad is still held make a chord: the first note goes on the cursor's step and the cursor moves on as usual; each further note goes on the same step, one track to the right. Hold the chord's pads together, release them, and play the next chord.

  • One Undo removes the whole chord.
  • A track that can't play the current instrument (a MIDI track for a sample instrument) ends the chord there.
  • Live recording (Rec while playing) already spreads a chord over the next free tracks.

docs.title: Slices to pattern
docs.text:
Chop a break, then press one key to get a pattern that plays it. On the Sample Playback screen (Slice or Beat Slice mode), open the More page (F6):

Key Does Steps (F4) How many steps the sample lasts. The guess is its length at the song tempo, rounded to 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars; turn the encoder if it guessed wrong (a 2-bar break at 92 BPM in a 140 BPM song reads as 4 bars). To Pattern (F5) Writes the slices on the pattern's current track (the one the cursor was on).
  • Slice i goes on the step nearest where it starts, as note 24 + i, with the steps in between empty, so each slice plays on to the next one. The trigs repeat every Steps steps to the end of the track.
  • The track is cleared first; it asks when the track had steps. Undo in the pattern editor brings them back.
  • A Slice instrument turns Beat Slice, so each note plays its own slice.
  • At another song tempo the slices play at their own speed and pitch (as REX loops do): a faster song cuts each slice short at the next trig, a slower one leaves a short gap after it. The pattern keeps its length; a sample longer than the track is placed once, cut at the track's end.
  • Slice first: Auto (F1) for drum breaks, Evenly (F2) for loops in time.

docs.title: The 2.x features (from upstream)
docs.text: The 2.x line brings the newer Tracker features to the original hardware. In short:

docs.title: Tracker Mini project compatibility
docs.text:
• Projects are saved in the Tracker 2.2.1 format: 16-track patterns, the three synth slots, track names and mutes for tracks 13–16.
  • Synth patches use the Mini's .patch files, stored with the project and in a library at Patches/<ENGINE>/. All 299 Mini factory patches load and save back unchanged.

docs.title: 16 tracks
docs.text:
• Tracks 13–16 work like MIDI tracks 9–12: notes, MIDI channels, CC A–F, pitch bend, velocity, mute and solo. Performance Play mode, Pattern length and Step repeater act on them too.
  • Pattern pages through all 16 tracks; Song shows a scrolling 12-track window. Fill, copy and paste work across all 16.

docs.title: Synth engines (instruments S1–S3)
docs.text:
• Three synth slots, played from any track as instruments S1–S3.
  • Engines: ACD (acid bass and lead, 24 dB and ladder-style filters, glide), VAP (virtual-analog poly, morphing oscillators, hard sync, 15 filter types, a 6-slot modulation matrix), PERC (a drum kit), FAT (unison supersaw), and in this fork DX7. WTFM patches load and save but stay silent ("not available").
  • Macros: FX columns A–F drive macros 1–6, and Volume drives macro 7.
  • Voices: a shared pool of 4 by default, adjustable in Config > General > Synth voices (1–8). If the audio gets close to its limit, only synth voices are cut; sample tracks never are.
  • Screens after the Mini's layout: Synth Parameters, Synth Macros, Edit Patch (sections on the pads; Save, Save As, Init), the Load Patch popup with Preview, and the synth level columns on Global Mixer page 3.
  • Exports include separate stems synth_1..3.wav.

docs.title: Export sample rate
docs.text: Config > General > Export sample rate: 44.1 kHz (default) or 44117 Hz. The Tracker's audio runs at 44,117 Hz. At 44.1 kHz, exported songs, patterns, stems and renders are converted to a standard 44,100 Hz WAV, so they play in time in any DAW. 44117 Hz writes the Tracker's own rate, as the original firmware does.

docs.title: Stereo samples
docs.text: Stereo WAVs keep both channels and play in stereo in one-shot, loop, slice and beat-slice modes; pan works as balance.

docs.title: CPU meter
docs.text: Config > General > CPU meter: Auto, Always or Off shows the audio load in the title bar.

docs.title: USB Storage mode
docs.text:
Config > USB > USB Storage: On shows the SD card on a connected computer as a USB drive, as on the Tracker Mini, so projects, samples and patches can be copied without taking the card out.

  • Playback stops and the project is saved first. Keep the power and the cable connected while files are copied.
  • To finish, eject the drive on the computer, then press Exit (or set the row back to Off). The project reloads from the card.
  • It's always Off after power-on. About 1 MB/s (full-speed USB). USB MIDI and the serial log keep working.
  • On Windows the Tracker may appear once as a new device (new COM/MIDI port).

docs.title: Performance mode
docs.text: The Performance screen plays effects live from the pads: 12 columns, each an effect type, with 3 stored values per column on the pad rows. The fork adds scenes with a crossfader, a bank of 16 scenes, master FX (DJ filter, tape stop) and MIDI CC columns that play an external synth's parameters.

docs.title: Basics (as in stock)
docs.text:
• Press Performance. Hold a pad to play that column's value on its row; release to go back. The top row shows what's playing.
  • Rec (edit mode): the encoder changes the value of the selected row. In the fork, a tapped row can be edited with the encoder without holding the pad.
  • Choosing a column's effect type (fork): in edit mode, Up / Down open a list of every type on the column's current one, on the left of the screen (the title names the column). Move with the encoder (Shift + a quick turn for bigger jumps) or Up / Down, then press OK (F8). Cancel (F7), Left / Right or Rec close it without changing anything (for MIDI CC, Left / Right move between its lists instead). Nothing is applied until OK, and the F keys don't switch track effects while the list is open. The row values stay when the new type has the same range (e.g. Volume to Panning); otherwise they're cleared as in stock. Stock stepped the type with Up / Down, applying each one on the way.

- The F keys turn the effects on or off per track (lit = on). Shift + F key mutes the track. Left / Right (outside edit mode) switch the F keys between tracks 1–8 and 9–16. In the fork the F keys are remembered: leaving the screen and coming back keeps them, and they're saved with the project (stock turns every track on again).

  • Effect types include Volume, Panning, Tune, Low-pass / High-pass / Band-pass, Delay and Reverb send, Start / End pos, Direction, the LFOs, Repeater, Play mode, Length, Bit depth and Overdrive, plus the fork's DJ filter, Tape stop and MIDI CC.

docs.title: Scenes and the crossfader
docs.text:
A scene stores a row for every column. The crossfader's two ends, A and B, each play a scene; the encoder (outside edit mode) or MIDI CC 63 fades between them.

  • Continuous values (volume, filters, sends …) fade smoothly. Filters cross over at the middle (a low-pass on A and a high-pass on B don't fight). Stepped effects (Repeater, Direction, Tape stop …) switch at the middle.
  • The title bar shows the pair (A 1 |------| B 2) and where the fader is. Rows of the scene on A are marked red, on B blue; the pad LEDs and the green (active) row follow the fader.
  • A pad pressed on a column the scenes drive takes it over: its row plays and turns green. The next fader move hands the column back to the scenes.

docs.title: Store and clear while playing
docs.text: Keys Does Shift + Left / Right Store the current pad rows into the scene on A / B. Delete + Left / Right Clear the scene on A / B. Hold pads + Shift / Delete + Left / Right Store / clear only the held columns.

docs.title: Which tracks get the effects
docs.text:
Storing a whole scene (Shift + Left / Right with no pad held) also stores which tracks have their effects on (the F keys). When that scene is loaded again, the F keys follow it:

  • putting it on A or B (from the bank page or a song slot),
  • moving the fader past the middle, to the scene on the other side.

So a song can have the drums in the Repeater in the verse and everything in the chorus. A scene stored before (or cleared with Delete) carries no F keys and leaves them as they are. Tapping an F key while a scene plays works as usual; the scene's setting comes back the next time the scene is loaded or the fader crosses the middle. Storing only some columns (pads held) doesn't change a scene's F keys. While a scene is open for editing (bank page, F3 Edit), the F keys show and change that scene's tracks; going back saves them and your live F keys come back.

docs.title: The scene bank
docs.text:
Press Performance again on the Performance screen to open the scene bank page: 16 scenes, with the ones on A and B marked.

Key Does Arrows, encoder or pads Select a scene. F1 Set A / F2 Set B Put the selected scene on the fader's A / B end. F3 Edit Open the scene on the Performance screen ("Editing scene N"): the pads set its rows, and you hear them as you go. Going back saves it. F4 Clear Clear the selected scene. F8 Back or Performance Back to playing.

Scenes can also be put on the fader by a song: see Song mode.

docs.title: Master FX
docs.text:
Two effect types act on the whole mix (after all tracks and synths, before the limiter), instead of on each track:

  • DJ filter: one value from −100 to +100. Below 0 a low-pass sweeping down, above 0 a high-pass sweeping up, 0 off. It's smoothed, so pads and the fader don't click, and it uses no CPU while off.
  • Tape stop: momentary. Hold its pad and the mix slows down to a stop over 1 or 2 steps, beats or bars (the row's value); release and it spins back up. It borrows free sample memory while it runs (shared with resampling), so it can refuse when memory is full.

Set them like any column: in edit mode, Up / Down open the type list; DJ filter and Tape stop are at the end.

docs.title: MIDI CC columns
docs.text:
A MIDI CC column plays a parameter of an external synth: one of a MIDI instrument's CC slots A–F, on that instrument's channel. Set it up in the type list: highlight MIDI CC, press Right to pick the MIDI instrument (shown with its preset name), Right again to pick the slot (shown with its CC name), then OK (F8).

  • The column is labelled with the instrument and the CC's name, e.g. MIDI 3 Cutoff. Which CC a slot sends is set on the MIDI instrument's parameters page, so change it there and the column follows.
  • Rows hold a value 0–127 (an empty row, ---, is off). A pad press sends its value; the fader, scenes and incoming CC send only when the value changes. Off, or leaving the screen, sends nothing, so the synth keeps its last value.
  • Several MIDI CC columns play at once, one per parameter. Two columns on the same slot are like two columns of one type: pressing one turns the other off.
  • Scenes fade each MIDI CC column on its own, so the fader (or a song's slot ramp) sweeps a synth's filter as it does a sample filter. A scene that doesn't drive the column leaves it at the other scene's value: a CC has no "off" value to fade to.
  • If the instrument's MIDI LFO is on the same slot, the column sets the LFO's Center, as a CC step FX does, and the LFO keeps swinging around it.

docs.title: Saved with the project
docs.text: The scene bank, the F keys (live and per scene), the master FX and MIDI CC types and the MIDI CC columns' instruments and slots are stored in perf_scenes.bin next to project.mt. Stock firmware and the Tracker Mini see those columns as empty and ignore the scenes.

docs.title: Remote control
docs.text: A Tracker running OpenTracker can be connected to a computer over USB and driven from it: as the simulator's front panel, by test scripts, or mirrored live on screen.

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
1. Connect the Tracker by USB.
  2. Config > USB > Remote control: On. It's Off again after every power-on.
  3. On Linux the Tracker appears as a serial port, usually /dev/ttyACM0. If it can't be opened, add your user to the group that owns it (uucp on Arch, dialout on Debian/Ubuntu).

One program at a time

The link shares the USB serial port with the diag log. Close serial terminals, loggers or anything else that holds the port open first.

A short press of the power switch ends remote control (holding it still powers off).

docs.title: Drive mode: scripts
docs.text:
tools/tracker_remote.py presses buttons and pads, turns the encoder, reads the Tracker's status (screen, transport, output level, CPU, the current notice), the text on screen, and takes screenshots. The Tracker's own controls keep working.

tools/tracker_remote.py /dev/ttyACM0 -c "tap PERFORMANCE; wait 300; expect-screen Performance; text; screenshot perf.png" \
    --out shots --log tracker.log
  • Scripts use the simulator's script language plus checks (expect-text, expect-sound, wait-for slot == 2 …). Ready-made ones are in tools/remote_scripts/; the same files run on the simulator in CI.
  • --log keeps everything the Tracker sends, including its telemetry lines. Check them with tools/telemetry_check.py log tracker.log.

Edit mode

In the Pattern screen's edit mode, the encoder and pads change the pattern. Turn edit mode off before running scripts that use them there.

docs.title: Live mirror
docs.text:
The simulator shows the Tracker's screen live and sends its window's keys and mouse to the Tracker:

build/sim/opentracker-sim --mirror /dev/ttyACM0

The Tracker sends each frame it draws (about 12 per second while playing).

docs.title: Panel mode
docs.text:
The Tracker becomes the simulator's front panel: its buttons, pads and encoder drive the simulator, and the simulator lights its pads.

build/sim/opentracker-sim --remote /dev/ttyACM0

The Tracker shows "Remote control: panel drives the simulator" and stops reacting to its own controls until the simulator quits or the cable is unplugged (it recovers within 2 s).

docs.title: Live resampling
docs.text: Record the master mix, one track (including the synth it plays) or Line in while the sequencer keeps playing, Octatrack-style. The take starts on the next bar and lasts 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 bars, or until you stop it. It lands in an instrument slot, ready to play, slice or re-record.

docs.title: Open the Resample screen
docs.text:
• While playing, press Sample Recorder. The Tracker asks "This will stop the pattern"; press Resample (F6) instead. The pattern keeps playing.
  • Shift + Sample Recorder arms, stops or cancels a take from any screen, with the Resample screen's current settings.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Column (key) Choices From (F1) Master (after the limiter), Track 1–8 (the track's sample voice plus the synth notes it plays, dry), Line in (with the recorder's channel mode). Length (F2) Manual (until you stop it, snapped to a bar) or 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 bars. Slices (F3) Off, Per beat, Per step (equal slices), Beat hits, Step hits (a slice only where a new hit starts, so empty steps stay empty). Into (F4) New (the next free instrument) or instrument 1–48 (re-record into it). Place on (F5) Off or Track 1–8: write the take onto a track. Gain, Monitor (F6, F7) Line in only: the recorder's input gain and monitoring. Record (F8) Arm: the take starts on the next bar (or with Play). Press again to stop at the next bar.

The right-hand column shows the take's state (Ready, Armed, Recording …) and, for Line in, a level meter.

docs.title: Where the take goes
docs.text:
• Into: New puts the take into the next free instrument above every loaded one, in stereo, so no playing sample moves. It's saved with the project.
  • Into: Instrument N re-records into N:
    • a take of the same length overwrites N in place, without a gap, and keeps N's settings, so a loop can be re-sampled take after take while it plays;
    • a take of another length isn't lost: it's saved as a new instrument, and a notice says so.
    • Arming into a slot that holds a sample asks once.
  • The take records into the free sample memory, which is reserved while it runs. The Sample Loader's memory bar counts it, and loading a sample during a take says why it can't.

docs.title: Slices and Place on
docs.text:
• With Slices on, the take becomes a Beat Slice instrument: note 24 + i (pad i + 1) plays slice i. At most 48 slices; the grid doubles until they fit.
  • Place on track N writes the take onto the track's first step, repeating every take length, or, when sliced, each slice on its own step, so the Performance FX (Repeater, Play mode, Direction, Start pos) work on it in time. Place on can be undone.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Resampling a track records it dry: no delay or reverb sends, no master FX.
  • The diag log on USB gets one line per take (frames, silent blocks, peak, input health), useful when a Line in take has dropouts.

docs.title: Song mode
docs.text:
The Song screen arranges patterns into a list of slots. The fork adds repeat counts, a Performance scene per slot, and fader ramps between two scenes, so a song can be arranged with performance changes without copying patterns.

The Song list has four columns: Pattern, Count, Scene and Ramp. In edit mode (Rec), Right moves from the list into the columns, Left back. Delete resets the selected value.

docs.title: Repeat counts
docs.text:
• Count plays the slot's pattern 1 to 16 times before the song moves on, so a section no longer needs duplicate slots. Set it with the encoder.
  • While playing, the playing slot shows its pass, for example 3/4.
  • Add Slot copies the count. Loop Pattern / Continue Song work as before (Continue leaves the slot at the end of the current pass).

docs.title: Scenes per slot
docs.text:
• Scene puts a scene from the scene bank on the crossfader's A end as the slot starts, with the fader at A. The encoder picks the scene, or - for none.
  • Shift + encoder adds a second scene for B (shown as 3>4).
  • A slot's scene plays on any screen, not only on the Performance screen, until Stop or the next slot.
  • A - slot (no scene): on the Performance screen what plays stays; on other screens the song's scene ends (FX off). To hold a scene across slots, set it on each slot.

docs.title: Ramps
docs.text:
A slot with a scene on B sweeps the fader from A to B. Ramp sets when:

Ramp The fader goes A → B … Slot across all the slot's passes Each across each pass, back to A as the next one starts First across the first pass, then stays on B Last, L2 … L15 across the last N passes (the choices follow the slot's Count) 1 … 128 across the slot's last N steps (Shift + encoder moves by 16)

Moving the fader yourself takes over until the next slot.

docs.title: Moving around
docs.text: • Song + Right jumps from the track grid straight to the Pattern list; Song + Left goes back into the grid (edit mode). Shift + Left / Right still sizes the grid selection.

docs.title: Saved with the project
docs.text: Counts, scenes and ramps are stored in song.bin next to project.mt. Stock firmware plays every slot once, without scenes.

docs.title: Exporting
docs.text:
File > Export > Song and Song Stems render the slots' scenes and ramps the way playback does. F7 Perf FX on the Export page turns this On / Off (On after every power-on); Off gives the stock export without Performance FX.

  • Stems get each track's Performance FX. The master FX (DJ filter, tape stop) act on the whole mix, so only the full-mix export (Song) has them.
  • Only what the song stores is rendered: where the fader or the pads were when you pressed Export doesn't matter, so the same song always exports the same way.
  • Pattern exports play no song slots, so they render without scenes.

docs.title: The Tracker doesn't start, or keeps restarting
docs.text:
• Go back to stock: put the stock image's file name (for example PolyendTracker_1.9.2.ptf) in /Firmware/ot_restore.txt on the card and power-cycle. This runs before the rest of OpenTracker. See Install and go back.
  • The update bootloader and the rear reset button are never touched by OpenTracker; the worst case is reflashing.

docs.title: "Restarted after a crash (stack overflow)"
docs.text:
OpenTracker has a stack guard: a protected memory area below the stack. If the stack ever overflows into it, the Tracker resets cleanly instead of silently corrupting memory, and after the restart it shows "Restarted after a crash (stack overflow)" for a few seconds. The diag log records "reset reason: core lockup".

  • Please report it as an issue, with what you were doing and, if possible, the diag log.
  • To run without the guard (for example to compare), create an empty file /Firmware/ot_noguard.txt.

docs.title: Sound problems
docs.text:
• Crackles or dropped notes when busy: check the CPU meter (Config > General > CPU meter). The voice limiter cuts synth voices first when the audio gets close to its limit; lowering Synth voices or synth polyphony helps.
  • A synth slot is silent and shows "not available": its model has no engine in this build (WTFM).
  • DX7 voice sounds different from a hardware DX7: report the voice (.syx file) in an issue; the engine is checked against Dexed, not hardware.

docs.title: The diag log and telemetry
docs.text:
Over USB, the Tracker also appears as a serial port with a diag log: boot messages, warnings, and every 5 seconds a telemetry line:

telemetry: render cyc/block min … avg … max … | loop max … ms | stack peak … B heap … B of … B (free … B) | rx restarts … stale …
  • render: audio CPU per 128-sample block (the budget is 522,240 cycles).
  • loop max: the slowest main-loop pass (UI, SD card).
  • stack peak / free: the deepest stack use since boot and what's left.
  • rx restarts / stale: Line in health (I2S input restarts and stale blocks).

Read it with any serial terminal, or capture it with tools/tracker_remote.py --log. tools/telemetry_check.py log FILE checks a captured log against the thresholds.
